sources.title: Ministry of External Relations: Cameroon e-Visa procedure
sources.publisher: Ministry of External Relations of Cameroon
sources.officialityEvidence: MINREX publishes this current entry-visa workflow on its official diplocam.cm domain and identifies evisacam.cm as the electronic service. It describes online submission, payment, review and an authorisation bearing a QR code.
sources.supportingExcerpt: une autorisation de délivrance de visa en ligne assortie d’un QR Code

sources.title: Prime Minister’s Office: July 2024 Cabinet Council on Cameroon e-Visa
sources.publisher: Services of the Prime Minister of Cameroon
sources.officialityEvidence: The Prime Minister’s Office publishes this Cabinet Council account on its official spm.gov.cm site. It confirms that travellers use evisacam.cm for the compulsory online visa-file process.
sources.supportingExcerpt: tout usager souhaitant se rendre au Cameroun doit obligatoirement soumettre son dossier en ligne.

sources.title: CEMAC: Member States
sources.publisher: Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa
sources.officialityEvidence: CEMAC’s official Commission site identifies its six current Member States, including Cameroon and the five mapped foreign CEMAC passport states.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Cameroun, le Congo, le Gabon, la Guinée Équatoriale, la République de Centrafrique et le Tchad.

sources.title: CEMAC Commission President interview on free movement
sources.publisher: Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa
sources.officialityEvidence: CEMAC’s official Commission website published this 2025 account. Its President states that visa-free free movement of citizens of the Member States is effective.
sources.supportingExcerpt: L’effectivité de la libre circulation des citoyens des pays membres de la CEMAC, sans visa, est une réalité indéniable.

sources.title: Presidency of Cameroon: Cameroon–Nigeria bilateral three-month visa exemption
sources.publisher: Presidency of the Republic of Cameroon
sources.officialityEvidence: The Presidency’s official prc.cm site records the bilateral provisions under which citizens of both States may reside in the other for three months with visa exemption. No termination was found in current official sources.
sources.supportingExcerpt: résider pendant trois mois dans l’un et l’autre pays, avec exemption de visa.

sources.title: Decree No. 2023/147 on implementation of alien entry, stay and exit law
sources.publisher: Presidency of the Republic of Cameroon
sources.officialityEvidence: The Presidency hosts the promulgated implementing decree on prc.cm. It defines short-stay visas for temporary visitors including tourists and sets the six-month upper validity limit.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The short-stay visa may be issued to the temporary visitor travelling as a tourist.

policies.title: CEMAC and Nigerian ordinary passports: Cameroon visa-free short visit
policies.summary: CEMAC’s current official material says visa-free free movement of its Member-State citizens is effective; this maps the five foreign CEMAC passports. A separate Presidency source directly supports the Cameroon–Nigeria bilateral exemption for a three-month stay. Neither source supports a visa-on-arrival or electronic-visa classification.
conditions: The CEMAC policy applies only to ordinary nationals of the five foreign Member States; it is not an extension of special, diplomatic or service-passport agreements. Admission, passport, health, security and border controls remain applicable.

The Cameroon–Nigeria bilateral source supports a stay or residence of up to three months with visa exemption. It is treated as a short-visitor exemption; its continued operation should be rechecked if the agreement or its implementing practice changes.
Do not apply this policy to employment, long-term residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or other special-document routes.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Cameroon online advance visa approval
policies.summary: Cameroon’s official Ministry and Prime Minister sources establish a compulsory online visa-file process for users travelling to Cameroon. MINREX says approval produces an online visa-issuance authorisation with a QR code before travel; the physical visa is then affixed at the border or competent mission. This is electronic advance approval, not an airport visa application or an ETA.
conditions: Apply through the official evisacam.cm portal before travel: create an account, enter the application, upload supporting documents, pay online and await processing by the competent diplomatic mission or consular post.

For applicants distant from a competent post, MINREX says the online QR-code visa-issuance authorisation permits travel and the visa is affixed at the entry border post. Applicants near the competent post may instead attend biometric enrolment. In both cases, approval precedes travel; the border step does not make this visa_on_arrival.

MINREX indicates normal processing within 72 hours after preregistration and express processing within 24 hours, but issuance is discretionary and individual documentary, health, security and admission requirements remain applicable.

The short-stay visa may serve temporary visitors travelling as tourists or businesspersons and cannot exceed six months. Work, study, residence, transit, family, diplomatic, official, service, courtesy, refugee and other special-document cases are separate.
The current review found no ordinary-passport nationality-wide arrival-visa cohort. The airport/border affixing mechanism is conditional on an approved online authorisation.

application.label: Cameroon official eVisa portal
application.processingTime: MINREX states 72 hours after preregistration for the normal process and 24 hours for express processing; neither guarantees grant.
steps: Create an account at the official evisacam.cm portal and complete the online visa application.
Upload the requested supporting documents and pay the required online fee.

Await the competent mission or consular post’s decision. Travel only with the issued QR-code visa-issuance authorisation, then complete visa affixing at the specified entry border post or competent mission.

conflicts.explanation: Cameroon’s current MINREX process requires a pre-travel online visa application and QR-code issuance authorisation; visa affixing at the border follows that approval and is not a visa-on-arrival application.

The current CEMAC visa-free scope is limited to its Member-State citizens and the Cameroon–Nigeria bilateral exemption does not establish a Malian ordinary-passport exemption. The current eVisa procedure therefore applies.

unresolved.reason: The reviewed current official sources establish foreigner visa procedure, CEMAC movement and issuance of Cameroonian travel documents, but do not directly establish a Cameroonian citizen’s entry or return right. Citizenship is not inferred from passport issuance or foreigner rules.
